title: The Creation of the Heavens, Earth, and Living Creatures
summary: Genesis 1:1-2:3 presents the creation and ordering of the heavens and earth. The passage moves from an unformed world to a populated environment of land, seas, sky, plants, animals, and humans, ending with the seventh day.

stepIntoStory:
The scene opens before any human city, road, field, or household appears. The narrative moves across the whole created order, from darkness and waters to light, sky, land, seas, vegetation, celestial lights, living creatures, and humans.

Living creatures fill the seas, sky, and land. The scene grows from an unformed setting into a populated world with plants, animals, birds, sea creatures, and humans.

source.audioScript: Genesis 16 begins inside Abram's household. Sarai has no child, and Hagar, her Egyptian servant, becomes part of the family conflict. situation: Abraham is sitting near the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day.
stepIntoStory:
The scene begins at Abraham's tent near the oaks of Mamre. It is the heat of the day, and Abraham is seated at the tent entrance.

Three visitors appear nearby. Abraham runs to meet them, offers water, rest, bread, curds, milk, and a prepared calf, and stands by while they eat.

The announcement turns the ordinary setting into a major story moment. Sarah, listening from the tent entrance, hears that she will have a son.

audioScript: Genesis 18 opens near the oaks of Mamre. Abraham is at the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day when three visitors appear. The details are physical and ordinary: water for feet, bread, curds, milk, and a calf prepared for a meal. Then the scene turns. Sarah, inside the tent, hears that she will have a son. The promise of Isaac moves from covenant speech into the living space of Abraham and Sarah's household.

audioScript: After the visitors eat near Mamre, they rise and look toward Sodom. Abraham walks with them, and the story slows into a conversation about the city. The questions move through numbers: fifty, forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty, and ten. This is not yet the city scene. stepIntoStory:
The scene begins at the city gate in the evening. Lot sees two messengers arrive, rises to meet them, and brings them into his house.

The night becomes dangerous inside the city. By morning, Lot is urged to leave with his family, and the messengers bring them out.

The escape route moves away from Sodom toward Zoar. Behind them, the cities of the plain are overthrown, and Abraham later looks down toward the smoke rising from the land.
